# OmniH2O Uses RGB+HybrIK or Vision Pro for Real-time Remote Operation, Does It Need to Convert Each Frame of SMPL Data via Gradient Descent into H1 Reference?

> **Current answer:** The project author does not need to provide explanations. Real-time deployment directly uses the global keypoint positions from the visual system output, as the strategy tracks sparse inputs (sparse inputs), not full-body motions (whole-body motions). The offline SMPL→H1 gradient retargeting is part of the training data preparation. The original thread did not publicly disclose the specific matrix transformation from RGB/HybrIK coordinates to Isaac Gym/robot world coordinates, so coordinate calibration still needs to be verified separately.

## Problem and symptoms

- Is it necessary to repeat the offline gradient retargeting of SMPL human data in real-time deployment in order to become a robot reference?
- The user sees the training data preprocessing converting SMPL motion via gradient descent into H1 reference, thus not knowing how the real-time visual input meets the same interface.

## Environment

- Human2humanoid/OmniH2O deployment context; Apple Vision Pro or RGB camera + HybrIK; original post did not provide software commit, frequency, or camera calibration parameters.

## Priority diagnostics

- Distinguish between the offline whole-body motion tracking and the online sparse keypoint tracking, which are not the same input path.
- Confirm that the real-time strategy consumes specific global keypoint positions, not the default reconstruction of full AMASS/SMPL motion.

## Possible causes

- The offline SMPL→H1 retargeting process used for full-body training is mistakenly considered a mandatory step in the real-time sparse input deployment.

## Attempts

- The original author asked how to obtain processed AMASS-like joint data in real-time; the project author clarified that the deployment does not require a full-body reference.

## Effective fixes

- Follow the project author's instructions, using global keypoint positions from Vision Pro or RGB+HybrIK as direct input to the real-time deployment, without repeating full-body motion retargeting in the real-time loop.

## Result

- The questioner replied that they now understand the difference between sparse input and whole-body retargeting.
